summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a patient with end-stage multiple myeloma, myelodysplastic syndrome, COPD, and a neobladder, was admitted for altered mental status and somnolence. Initial evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection with Enterococcus sensitive only to vancomycin, prompting a switch from cefepime. His confusion improved with treatment and hydration, though it waxed and waned. Hypercalcemia was present but resolved with IV fluids. Imaging showed no acute intracranial process, stable abdominal aortic aneurysm, and improvement in prior lung opacity. Hip X-ray revealed severe osteoarthritis and lytic lesions consistent with myeloma progression. He was discharged home with a plan to return for continued IV vancomycin, with stable mental status and no acute complications.
